subject: Late-binding SKU template & co-sell handoff for multi-cloud listings
messages:
From: CloudMarketOps <ops@cloudmarketops.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: MarketplaceOps <marketplace@cloudmarketops.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:12:00Z
Subject: Pilot SKU approach for marketplace syndication

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the sync today. As promised, attaching a short pilot proposal for how we could syndicate Redwood offerings across AWS/Azure/GCP using a late-binding SKU model. High-level asks:

- Start with a small canonical SKU set (Core, Scale, Enterprise) and allow cloud listings to attach region-specific entitlements during listing time.
- We think a late-binding SKU will keep SKU proliferation low while enabling co-sell pricing at the region/partner level.
- Need a list of required metadata (SKU code, billing granularity, entitlement flags, supported regions, recommended instance families).

See attached: pilot-sku-proposal.pdf (3 pages).

Can you share a first-pass template we can use to map to each cloud’s listing schema? Also looping in MarketplaceOps on our side (cc) to confirm any platform constraints.

Best,
Sam Patel
CloudMarketOps
Attachment: pilot-sku-proposal.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: CloudMarketOps <ops@cloudmarketops.com>, MarketplaceOps <marketplace@cloudmarketops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot SKU approach for marketplace syndication

Sam — thanks for the concise brief. I kicked off an internal draft that maps out a single late-binding template we can populate per-cloud and per-region. Attaching sku-template-draft.xlsx.

Key assumptions in the template:
- SKU tiers: Core / Pro / Enterprise (carrier-neutral).
- Billing: per-second meter + monthly commitment option (where cloud allows).
- Entitlements: KV cache retention, dedicated pool flag (for Dedicated customers), private deployment toggle.
- Region gating: Canary region + full-regions list; each cloud can override which regions count as canary.

Immediate asks for you / MarketplaceOps:
- Confirm required metadata fields for Azure listings (SKU id length, allowed characters).
- Any constraints around pricing override vs. marketplace list price for co-sell subsidies.

I'll schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the template. Marissa — can you take lead on co-sell enablement pack items? Karthik — please flag procurement/legal hooks we need to include.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Director, Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachment: sku-template-draft.xlsx (XLSX, 220KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, CloudMarketOps <ops@cloudmarketops.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot SKU approach for marketplace syndication

Thanks Jonas — reviewed the draft. A few pragmatic changes from GTM / co-sell perspective:

- Split "Pro" into Pro-Standard and Pro-Plus for marketplaces that require narrower SKU bands (helps meet Azure’s SKU tag limits).
- Add a small co-sell enablement pack per SKU: 1-pager sell sheet, 2 customer case studies, 1-page pricing comparator. We should version these by cloud if the listed price differs.
- Canary region suggestion: start with us-east-1 (AWS), eastus (Azure), us-central1 (GCP) and gate additional regions after telemetry for 2 weeks.

I'm drafting a co-sell checklist (co-sell-checklist-v1.md) to attach to the template: marketplace listing assets, partner contacts, discount bands, required SOC2 statements, and sample legal text for co-sell referrals.

Marissa
VP, GTM Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachment: co-sell-checklist-v1.md (MD, 8KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T14:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot SKU approach for marketplace syndication

Quick procurement/legal note: Azure’s listing flow enforces a per-SKU entitlement schema that is stricter than AWS/GCP. If we push late-binding too far (e.g., permitting arbitrary entitlement flags at list time), Azure will require separate SaaS offers for materially different entitlements. Suggestion:

- For Azure, surface two SKU families only (Core/Enterprise) and use offer metadata + ARM template parameters for per-deployment entitlements.
- For AWS/GCP, we can use late-binding tags more liberally.

Also attaching a short doc with Azure constraints I pulled from a recent partner onboarding: azure-entitlement-notes.docx.

If legal needs to pre-approve the sample ARM parameter text I can route it. Ben — can you check whether Dedicated-pool entitlements require a separate offer on AWS?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Technical Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachment: azure-entitlement-notes.docx (DOCX, 54KB)

From: Azure Partner Team <azure-partner@contoso.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudMarketOps <ops@cloudmarketops.com>
Date: 2027-05-06T08:50:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot SKU approach for marketplace syndication

Jonas / Marissa — appreciate the draft and the call proposal. A couple of asks from our side:

- Please provide the canonical SKU-to-offer mapping (spreadsheet) and the final ARM parameters we expect customers to set at deployment.
- For co-sell, we need the listed price and the partner-facing discount band documented; that determines whether our field will push deals.
- We will need a signed co-sell MSA template before we enable any referral incentives. Is there a DocuSign link you prefer?

On timing: if you can deliver the finalized template + one sample listing by next Friday (2027-05-14), we can validate in our test tenant and confirm co-sell enablement.

Regards,
Nina Chao
Azure Partner Program | Contoso Cloud

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Azure Partner Team <azure-partner@contoso.com>, CloudMarketOps <ops@cloudmarketops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T17:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Late-binding SKU template & co-sell handoff for multi-cloud listings

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps below (tl;dr at top):

TL;DR
- We will adopt the late-binding template but restrict SKU variance on Azure to two families (Core / Enterprise).
- Marissa: finalize the co-sell enablement pack (Marissa owner).
- Karthik: route the ARM parameter wording to Legal for Azure-specific language (Karthik owner).
- MarketplaceOps/CloudMarketOps: we will handoff finalized template + sample listing by 2027-05-14.

Decisions / Notes
- SKU families: Core, Pro-Standard, Pro-Plus, Enterprise for AWS & GCP. Azure will list Core / Enterprise and accept per-deployment ARM params to enable extra entitlements.
- Canary regions: us-east-1 (AWS), eastus (Azure), us-central1 (GCP). Two-week telemetry gate.
- Billing model: default per-second with optional monthly commitment. Cloud-specific pricing overrides allowed but must be documented in the co-sell pack.
- Attachments to finalize: sku-template-draft.xlsx (master), co-sell-checklist-v1.md, ARM parameter snippet (Karthik to produce), and sample listing payload for each cloud.

Action items and owners
- Marissa Cole: co-sell enablement pack and pricing comparator (due 2027-05-12).
- Karthik Iyer: ARM parameter text and legal touchpoint (due 2027-05-11).
- Jonas Weber: prepare the sample listing payloads and push to CloudMarketOps by 2027-05-14.
- Ben Carter / Kimberly Park: verify Dedicated-pool treatment across AWS offers (quick check; Ben owner).

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-marketplace-syndication (template folder), HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/4821, DocuSign template: https://www.docusign.com/templates/abc-marketplace-co-sell

If nobody objects, I’ll hand off the draft files to MarketplaceOps tomorrow morning and set up a short review with Azure test tenant next week.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachment: sku-template-draft.xlsx (finalized pending, XLSX, 230KB)
